title: Counterexample
description: A structured counterexample from a verification failure (ESBMC or the native backend)

function.description: Name of the function whose verification query failed

values.description: Map of source names (or, under the ESBMC backend, $esbmc$-prefixed internal variable names) to counterexample values. Under the native backend a field of a struct, enum, Option or Result parameter is named <param>.<slot> (an enum's discriminant is slot 0), with a :bool, :f32, :f64 or :<bits> suffix when the function reads that slot at two sorts; bool values are true or false. Under the native backend an object a counterexample lists only as an address (a Vec, String or struct held in a field, or an element of a Vec of them) has an entry <position>.contents whose value is unconstrained (the failing claim never reads through the address, so any contents reproduce the failure) or unlisted (it does, or the verifier cannot tell, and the contents are not listed). An object the function read through is listed under its position when the verifier can: <position>.len and <position>[<i>] for a Vec or String (a nested element is named <position>[<i>][<j>]), <position>.<slot> for a struct

violation.description: Description of the violated contract clause, or of the internal check that failed when blame is "None"

vow_id.description: Function-local ID of the violated vow clause, or a reserved verifier sentinel when the failure cannot be attributed to a user-authored vow

offset.description: Byte offset of the vow clause

length.description: Byte length of the vow clause

source.description: Source location of the violated vow clause, identical in both compilers; null when the failure cannot be attributed to a vow clause

blame.description: Who is responsible for the violation

call_sites.description: Caller locations relevant to caller-blame failures

violating_args.description: Callee parameters and caller argument spans for caller-blame precondition failures

value.description: Counterexample value for the caller argument. The empty string means the value could not be statically recovered; arg_offset and arg_length still identify the caller argument.

replay_reason.description: Human-readable explanation for an aborted, diverged, or skipped replay
